clue.text: Manor erected by old money, guarantees of quality

parts.note: a manor house is often called a hall
marks were the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A manor house built with inherited wealth, offered as proof of high standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected by' reads as building, but only joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamps struck on gold and silver certify purity, so the word stands for any mark of excellence.

clue.text: Author about to receive printout

indicators.note: the author's name goes round the next piece, as if standing about it

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist
to cop something is slang for to get or receive it

explanation.surface: A writer is about to be handed a printed copy of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the containment signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper copy of computer data is called a printout, as opposed to a file on screen.

clue.text: Spice up vile new concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook livens up a nasty new mixture with spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice up' sits at the front as a verb phrase; 'concoction' is the anagram signal, fitting the cooking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To spice something up is to make it livelier and more interesting.

clue.text: Full of woes, see me not shifting responsibility

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are filled with the next piece, which sits inside them
the letters of 'me not' shift into a new order

parts.note: ills are troubles or woes

explanation.surface: Someone miserable claims nobody else is taking on the burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges ME NOT into MTONE, and 'Full of' puts ILLS inside it after the M; 'see' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone round the neck is a heavy burden, a weighty duty one cannot shake off.

clue.text: French poet sounds a mindless brute

indicators.note: the poet's name is pronounced like the brute's name

parts.note: Rambo, the violent action hero of the films, used as a byword for a thuggish tough guy

explanation.surface: A French poet's name seems to call up a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: In French, the poet's name is said roughly 'ram-BOH', close to the film hero Rambo.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rimbaud was a nineteenth-century French Symbolist writer of verse.

clue.text: Biblical land has appeal to girl I've just met

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
from the West Side Story song 'Maria': 'I've just met a girl named Maria'

explanation.surface: A Biblical region holds charm for a newly encountered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Samaria was a region of ancient Israel named in the Old and New Testaments.

clue.text: Seedy operative may get worse

indicators.note: the word that follows may turn into a different word by rearranging, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A shady agent might deteriorate further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' suggests disreputable, but here it means one who deals in seeds: a person planting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer scattering seed in a field is the planting worker the clue describes.

clue.text: Mass fight contained by NCO

indicators.note: the fight sits inside the officer's letters

parts.note: a sergeant major, abbreviated SM, is a non-commissioned officer
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A big brawl is broken up by a sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large crowd or throng, as of bees or people.

clue.text: Cat has three minutes with boxer collection

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip
a professional boxing round lasts three minutes

explanation.surface: A cat spends three minutes in the ring with a fighter, then a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British informal collection of money among colleagues, for a leaving present say.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal gathering of money from a group, such as an office.

clue.text: Smelling worse in private

explanation.surface: Something smells worse in the barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling, so this is smellier; and a soldier who serves in the ranks, such as a private, is a ranker.

clue.text: Return from bar to party

indicators.note: the word for a bar is read in the return direction, backwards

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: Someone goes back from the pub to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a metal rod; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively celebration, a festive gathering with drink and dancing.

clue.text: Like chimps? Chap can catch a million, going to African country

indicators.note: the man is able to catch the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a chap is a man
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: A man might seize a million and head off to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like chimps?' is a question because chimps are only one example of the class; 'going to' is a link joining the stolen pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees suckle their young and are warm-blooded, so they belong to the class of mammals.

clue.text: Article put in containers by army: this needs two packs

indicators.note: the article is put inside the containers

parts.note: cans are containers
A is the indefinite article
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier is packing goods into tins for the troops, who carry two rucksacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' suggests backpacks, but it means packs of cards; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two full decks.

clue.text: Touching, Samuel's display of conscience

parts.note: RE means concerning or about, as touching does
Samuel Morse, inventor of the Morse code

explanation.surface: Samuel's moving show of guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' reads as moving, but it means 'regarding', giving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt and deep regret shown after wrongdoing is the outward sign of a pricked conscience.

clue.text: Fundamental course that may get you set up for life

definitions.text: that may get you set up for life

parts.note: primordial means basic, existing from the beginning
soup is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A basic course of study that will make you financially secure for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up for life' suggests wealth, but it means starting life on Earth: organic molecules in early seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists theorise that the first living cells arose from a broth of chemicals in the early oceans.

clue.text: Try to preserve value of finger ring

parts.note: the index finger is the forefinger
a link is a ring of a chain

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to keep a finger ring from losing worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Index-linking ties pensions or wages to inflation so that their real worth is maintained.

clue.text: Sounding a little tipsy, disregarding any other seafood

indicators.note: a slightly drunk speaker slurs s into sh, so the word comes out sounding different

parts.note: selfish means caring only for oneself and not about others

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk person ignores everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'selfish' with a drunken slur and it comes out as the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, oysters and prawns are food taken from the sea in shells.

clue.text: Caution: one easily shocked about enclosure

indicators.note: the prude goes round, or about, the next piece

parts.note: a prude is easily offended by impropriety
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure written on letters

explanation.surface: A warning: a prim person is upset about a fenced area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' suggests a fenced space, but it is the abbreviation ENC from letters, which sits inside PRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is carefulness in avoiding risk, a synonym of wariness.

clue.text: Its doors are open daily in the lead-up to Christmas

definitions.text: Its doors are open daily in the lead-up to Christmas

parts.words: Its doors are open daily in the lead-up to Christmas
parts.note: sounds like a shop with festive opening hours, but describes a card with little flaps, one opened each December day

explanation.surface: A store is open every day before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: This card or box has numbered windows, one opened each day from 1 to 24 December.

clue.text: Time to lock up old abbey site

parts.note: to intern is to confine, especially in wartime

explanation.surface: It is time to secure an ancient monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey in the Wye Valley, Wales; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern in Monmouthshire is famous for its ruined medieval abbey, subject of a Wordsworth poem.

clue.text: He decides, having arrived, to eat snack

indicators.note: eating takes the snack inside, so it goes into the abbreviation

parts.note: arr. is the abbreviation for arrived, as on timetables
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: Someone arriving decides to have a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a judge or referee who settles disputes.

clue.text: Why king is drunk?

indicators.note: the letters are in a drunken jumble, reordered

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Someone asks why the monarch is tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges WHY, K and IS; the whole clue suggests the answer as the reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit distilled from malted grain is the drink that would explain a tipsy monarch.

clue.text: Spell with endless suffering: there are several sides to it

definitions.text: there are several sides to it

parts.note: a hex is a curse or spell

indicators.note: the word for suffering loses its last letter

parts.note: agony is great suffering

explanation.surface: A magic curse bringing unending pain, a complex matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the final Y of AGONY; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane figure with six straight edges; 'several' is fair for six.

clue.text: Novelist making huge amount? Knock one zero off!

indicators.note: one O, which looks like zero, is struck out of the huge number

parts.note: a googol is ten to the power of a hundred

explanation.surface: A writer earns a fortune and gets told to drop a nought.
explanation.walkthrough: A googol is written as 1 followed by 100 zeros; removing one O from GOOGOL gives the Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer of fiction, author of Dead Souls.

clue.text: Overdue book was stimulating

parts.note: elated, as a past-tense verb, means made cheerful or exhilarated

explanation.surface: A library book returned late was exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belated has come later than expected, like a late birthday card.

clue.text: City in Kentucky, also outside

indicators.note: the word for also goes outside, around, the state abbreviation

parts.note: too means also
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: There is a city in the US state as well as beyond it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like the container signal for Kentucky but is a link; the containing is done by 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

clue.text: The worst nettles may be very near

explanation.surface: The nastiest nettles could be close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettles sting, so the worst would be most painful; and near is old slang for mean, so very near means most miserly.

clue.text: Definitely confirm one's at home with family

parts.note: when one is at home, one is in
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Someone finalises plans while at home with relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: To ink in is to go over pencil in ink, making an arrangement firm; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing over a provisional pencilled entry in ink makes it fixed rather than tentative.

clue.text: Countryman's last to call on union

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it after

parts.note: a yoke is a bond or union, as of oxen yoked together

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A rural man is the final one to visit a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks as if it belongs to 'Countryman's', but it picks the L ending 'call'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated rustic, a country bumpkin.

clue.text: Where the only way is down, as Pooh found?

definitions.text: Where the only way is down, as Pooh found?

parts.words: Where the only way is down, as Pooh found?
parts.note: every direction from the top of the world is south; Winnie-the-Pooh finds it on an expedition in A.A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A place one can only descend from, as the bear discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: In Winnie-the-Pooh, Pooh goes on an 'expotition' and finds a pole that Christopher Robin declares the one the expedition sought.
explanation.definitionFit: At the northernmost point of the globe, every direction leads south, which maps show as down.
